q22527.en: Keeping the safe distance prevents a collision with the vehicle in front.

explain.short: If the car ahead brakes suddenly, the gap gives you time to react and stop. That is the whole point of the safe distance.
explain.rule: You keep the safe distance to avoid a rear-end crash (tamponamento) with the vehicle in front. It is not about head-on or side crashes.
explain.trap: 'evita la collisione' (avoids the collision) is exactly the purpose, so nothing is wrong here.

sceneParams.caption: Enough gap: you stop before the car ahead
lines: Your gap gives time to stop
No crash into the car ahead

q22528.en: The driver must judge the safe distance also on the basis of the speed of the vehicle they are driving.

explain.short: The faster you go, the more road you cover while you react and brake. So the gap must grow with your speed.
explain.rule: The safe distance (distanza di sicurezza) must let you stop without hitting the vehicle ahead. It grows with speed, slow reflexes, traffic, bad weather, hills and bends, the type and state of your vehicle, brakes, tyres and load.
explain.trap: 'anche' (also) means speed is one of several factors; it does count.

sceneParams.caption: Faster car: bigger gap needed

q22529.en: The driver must adjust the safe distance also according to their own reflexes.

explain.short: Slow reflexes mean a longer reaction time, so you travel further before braking. A slower driver needs a bigger gap.
explain.rule: The safe distance (distanza di sicurezza) must let you stop without hitting the vehicle ahead. It grows with speed, slow reflexes, traffic, bad weather, hills and bends, the type and state of your vehicle, brakes, tyres and load.
explain.trap: 'prontezza di riflessi' (quickness of reflexes) is about the driver, and the driver counts.

sceneParams.caption: Slower reflexes: keep a bigger gap

q22530.en: The safe distance must be set also according to the traffic conditions.

explain.short: In heavy or irregular traffic the cars ahead may brake often and suddenly. You must leave a gap that fits the traffic.
explain.rule: The safe distance (distanza di sicurezza) must let you stop without hitting the vehicle ahead. It grows with speed, slow reflexes, traffic, bad weather, hills and bends, the type and state of your vehicle, brakes, tyres and load.
explain.trap: 'condizioni del traffico' (traffic conditions) is one of the real factors.

sceneParams.caption: Busy, stop-and-go traffic: keep a safe gap
lines: Adapt your gap to the traffic

q22531.en: The safe distance must be set also according to the road's layout (bends, uphill and downhill stretches).

explain.short: Downhill you need more road to stop, and on bends you see less. So the shape and slope of the road matter.
explain.rule: The safe distance (distanza di sicurezza) must let you stop without hitting the vehicle ahead. It grows with speed, slow reflexes, traffic, bad weather, hills and bends, the type and state of your vehicle, brakes, tyres and load.
explain.trap: 'andamento planoaltimetrico' is a hard word: it just means the bends and the ups and downs of the road.

sceneParams.caption: Downhill and bends: you need a bigger gap

q22532.en: The safe distance must be set also according to the weather conditions.

explain.short: Rain, ice, snow or fog make braking longer or let you see less. In bad weather the gap must be bigger.
explain.rule: The safe distance (distanza di sicurezza) must let you stop without hitting the vehicle ahead. It grows with speed, slow reflexes, traffic, bad weather, hills and bends, the type and state of your vehicle, brakes, tyres and load.
explain.trap: 'condizioni atmosferiche' (weather conditions) is a real factor.

q22536.en: The safe distance to keep from a snow plough at work is 20 metres.

explain.short: A snow plough at work throws snow and moves slowly and unpredictably. The law says to stay at least 20 m behind it.

q22541.en: On an out-of-town road with one lane in each direction, goods vehicles with a total mass over 3.5 tonnes that are banned from overtaking must keep at least 100 metres between them.

q22542.en: The safe distance must be set also according to the type of fuel the engine uses.

explain.short: Petrol, diesel or gas does not change how fast you react or brake. Fuel type has nothing to do with the safe distance.

q22577.en: The safe distance can be shorter than the distance covered during the reaction time.

explain.short: If the gap is shorter than your reaction distance, you hit the car ahead before you even start braking. It must be at least that long.
explain.rule: Reaction distance (spazio percorso nel tempo di reazione) is the road you cover from seeing a danger until you start braking, about 1 second. The safe distance must be at least this long, and it can be longer.
explain.trap: 'può essere inferiore' (can be shorter) is the trap: the reaction distance is the minimum.

sceneParams.caption: Never shorter than your reaction distance

q22578.en: The minimum safe distance at 30 km/h is about 9 metres.

explain.short: In about 1 second of reaction at 30 km/h you travel about 9 m. That is the minimum gap.
explain.rule: The minimum safe distance is about the road covered in 1 second of reaction (roughly speed in km/h divided by 3.6). Quiz values: 30 km/h ≈ 9 m, 50 ≈ 14 m, 100 ≈ 28 m, 130 ≈ 36 m, 150 ≈ 42 m.
explain.trap: 'circa 9 metri' is the official value for 30 km/h; smaller numbers are the trap.

sceneParams.caption: 30 km/h: minimum gap about 9 m

explain.short: When you are distracted you see dangers late and react late. That can easily lead to a crash.
explain.rule: Distraction causes accidents. The phone, lighting a cigarette, looking for radio or device controls all take your eyes and mind off the road, and even a few seconds are dangerous.
explain.trap: 'può essere causa' (can be a cause) is simply true.

sceneParams.caption: Distracted driver: late reaction, crash risk

q22589.en: Driver distraction can be caused by switching on the mobile phone.

explain.short: Switching on or using the phone takes your eyes and mind off the road. It is a typical distraction.
explain.rule: Distraction causes accidents. The phone, lighting a cigarette, looking for radio or device controls all take your eyes and mind off the road, and even a few seconds are dangerous.
explain.trap: 'accensione del cellulare' (switching on the phone) is a real distraction.

sceneParams.caption: Phone in hand: eyes off the road

q22590.en: Driver distraction can be caused by lighting a cigarette.

explain.short: Lighting a cigarette uses your hands and eyes. For those seconds you are not watching the road.
explain.rule: Distraction causes accidents. The phone, lighting a cigarette, looking for radio or device controls all take your eyes and mind off the road, and even a few seconds are dangerous.
explain.trap: 'accensione di una sigaretta' (lighting a cigarette) is a real distraction.

sceneParams.caption: Lighting a cigarette: hands and eyes busy

q22591.en: Driver distraction can be caused by looking for the controls of the radio or other electronic devices.

explain.short: Looking for buttons on the radio, navigator or other devices takes your eyes off the road.
explain.rule: Distraction causes accidents. The phone, lighting a cigarette, looking for radio or device controls all take your eyes and mind off the road, and even a few seconds are dangerous.
explain.trap: 'ricerca dei comandi' (looking for the controls) is a real distraction.

sceneParams.caption: Searching for radio buttons: eyes off the road

q22592.en: Driver distraction is not caused by using the "mobile phone".

explain.short: Using the phone is one of the main causes of distraction. The statement says the opposite.
explain.rule: Distraction causes accidents. The phone, lighting a cigarette, looking for radio or device controls all take your eyes and mind off the road, and even a few seconds are dangerous.
explain.trap: 'non è determinata' (is not caused) turns a true fact into a false one.

sceneParams.caption: The phone IS a big distraction

q22593.en: Driver distraction is not a danger if it lasts only a few seconds.

explain.short: In a few seconds a car covers many metres: at 50 km/h about 14 m every second. Even a short distraction is dangerous.
explain.rule: Distraction causes accidents. The phone, lighting a cigarette, looking for radio or device controls all take your eyes and mind off the road, and even a few seconds are dangerous.
explain.trap: 'pochi secondi' (a few seconds) sounds harmless, but it is not.

sceneParams.caption: Even a few seconds blind is dangerous
lines: A few seconds: many metres blind
